message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported record third-quarter results for the period ended 2026-07-31, with revenue of $1.85 billion that grew 36.54 per cent on a year earlier and net income of 397 million that grew 107.85 per cent, alongside total assets of 11.92 billion and shareholders equity of 6.57 billion [D1]. The quarter carried a gross margin of 65.87 per cent and a net margin of 21.51 per cent [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue of 1.35 billion rose 43.09 per cent and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue of 501 million rose 21.6 per cent, lifting segment operating income from 338 million to 613 million, a gain of 81.36 per cent [D1]. For the quarter ending 2026-10-31 the company guided revenue to $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and earnings per share to $3.34 to $3.40 on a diluted share count of 172 million, with the mid point of the revenue range representing growth of 37 per cent [D1].

What the market is arguing about is durability and the shape of the constraint, with analysts pressing on whether the order levels are sustainable and whether the guidance is capped by component supply [D3]. Management's answer is that demand is not the limiter and that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters, with the supply situation likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Management also cautioned that the one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 artificially pulled up profitability and will not repeat, which raises the comparison bar for future periods [D3]. On valuation the shares carry a forward price to earnings multiple of 20.66 against a trailing multiple of 45.89, a gap that assumes the earnings growth delivered in the latest quarter continues [D5].

The plan is therefore to stay with the uptrend, which remains intact with the trend state marked as an uptrend and the close at 333.42 above the 20 day average of 330.47, the 50 day average of 326.21 and the 200 day average of 289.31, while the relative strength index of 54.21 and the average true range of 11.05 describe a market that is neither stretched nor asleep [D5]. Exposure should be added only on a move through the immediate resistance at 366.41, which carries a strength of 3, and reviewed if the 300.87 lower edge of the support band, whose strength is 59, gives way [D5]. Because supply is the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters, position size should be set against the guided range rather than against order momentum [D3]. The evidence to watch is the quarter ending 2026-10-31 against revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40, a gross margin at or above 65.87 per cent, segment operating income growth at or above 81.36 per cent, Communications Solutions Group revenue above 1.35 billion and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue above 501 million [D1].
